task: Produce a concise historical decision record for the Council meeting of 27 June 2024. Identify the draft, sponsors, vote, actual reporting action and its limits. Attribute the sponsors’ rationale and Algeria’s voting explanation. State exactly whether and where their positions overlapped, and what important difference persisted.
roles: United States and Japan sponsors’ desk

public.text: At meeting S/PV.9672, the President identified draft S/2024/500 as submitted by Japan and the United States. The draft was adopted as resolution 2739 (2024) by 12 votes in favour, none against and three abstentions. Algeria, China and the Russian Federation abstained.

Operative paragraph 1 of resolution 2739 extends the Secretary-General’s reporting request under paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) until 15 January 2025. The resolution also reiterates its demand that the Houthis cease attacks on merchant and commercial vessels and release the Galaxy Leader and its crew. It urges caution, restraint and diplomatic efforts. The adopted text contains no new authorization of military action or expansion of the reporting authority.

owned.text: Speaking for the United States and Japan after the vote, Mr. Wood explained that extending the Secretary-General’s reporting would provide the Council with accurate and timely information for future deliberations on the Houthi attacks. He said attacks threatened commerce and the flow of humanitarian assistance. Both co-sponsors voted in favour.

Mr. Bendjama said Algeria abstained, consistent with its January vote. It continued to value the Secretary-General’s monthly reports on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels for keeping the Council informed. Algeria attributed its abstention to concerns over implementation of resolution 2722 (2024) and what it regarded as misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign countries’ territory.

rubric.rule: Identify adoption as resolution 2739 (2024), give the exact 12–0–3 tally and identify Algeria, China and Russia as the abstaining members.
Name draft S/2024/500 and identify both Japan and the United States as its sponsors.
State that the Council extended the Secretary-General’s reporting request in paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) through 15 January 2025.
Attribute to the sponsors the aim of keeping the Council accurately and promptly informed about the attacks for future deliberations.
Attribute Algeria’s abstention to concern about implementation of resolution 2722, specifically perceived misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence involving attacks on sovereign territory.

Explicitly connect the sponsors and Algeria to their shared view that continued Secretary-General reporting keeps the Council informed, while distinguishing Algeria’s abstention on the resolution from rejection of the reporting itself. A list of parallel positions without a discernible comparison is insufficient.
Explicitly preserve that extending the reporting request conferred no new authorization of military action. Do not present a delegation’s legal view as a Council finding.
